text:
Liam Ohgren came to Vancouver as one of the pieces in the Quinn Hughes trade, and 24 games into his first full season as a Canuck he has six goals and 10 points in about 14 minutes a night. The goals are ahead of the chances: he has scored 2.5 more than his shots were worth, and he's shooting 16.7% against a range our numbers put nearer 13%.

The other side of the ledger runs the opposite way. Vancouver has scored 4.9 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him points. That usually swings back. The process, though, is thin: his team takes 37.8% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five when he's out there. Evolving-Hockey had the same story last season, with his line creating very little and his linemates among the weakest in the league.

What he does bring is a shot. His top speed reads 89 mph, 87th percentile, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has 53% of his shots coming off the rush. He's quiet lately (three points in 10 games).
